notes: As stated (3 or more digits) false: A056142_three_digits_false (n = 101, a(101) = 101101). Corrected (4 or more digits) proved: A056142.A056142_conjecture: for n with >= 4 decimal digits, a n is a palindrome iff Nat.digits 10 n is constant. Route: word_reduction/fp_unique (palindrome forces digits = image of the fixed-point word X, X_1 = a, X_2 = b, block m of X = reverse of X_1..X_m), S_of_pal (palindrome gives X_(d+i) = X_i, i < d), not_S (no such near-square for r >= 4: kernel decide for r < 106, strong induction via block transfer otherwise), digits_a. Axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Outside Lean: none (data terms checked by certificate/check_A056142.py only).

sources.cite: OEIS A056142, D. Wasserman comment (2005) and F. T. Adams-Watters conjecture (2006)
sources.what: 3 digits: palindrome iff n is; 4-5 digits: repdigits only (no proof); conjecture for 3 or more digits

prior_art.note: Literal statement refuted by the entry's own 3-digit comment; the 4-or-more-digit version is new here.
